attacks.claim: Customer documents and derived data (chunks, embeddings, prompts) must stay in the EU under DPAs, but the plan sends them to Nimbus Vector Store, which is provisioned in us-east-2, and only generation is pinned to eu-west-1. Retrieval chunks and embeddings would leave the EU from week 2 onward.
attacks.evidence: "Vector Store is in public preview and currently provisioned in us-east-2, with EU regions on Nimbus's GA roadmap."

attacks.claim: Zero data retention is claimed only for the generation API. Nothing states ZDR or equivalent DPA coverage for embed-3 or the Vector Store preview, so the derived-data retention obligation is unverified for those services.
attacks.evidence: "Zero data retention is enabled on our org account (signed addendum, ref NMB-ZDR-2291)." / ABSENT: ZDR or DPA terms covering embed-3 and Vector Store

attacks.claim: Week 3 irreversibly destroys the rollback path: the A100 reservation is released and fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters are deleted before any tenant is cut over (week 4) and before the regression suite has run. If Nimbus quality or latency fails, there is no way back to vLLM.
attacks.evidence: "release the A100 reservation ... and delete fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters from object storage"

attacks.claim: The release gate is the 4,100-case regression eval suite, which the artifact explicitly defers to week 6+, after cutover. Quality parity is supported only by a 25-question blind comparison, which is far too small to satisfy the stated gate.
attacks.evidence: "the full regression suite run moves to post-migration hardening (week 6+) rather than blocking cutover"

attacks.claim: Replacing LoRA per-practice adapters with system prompts is an unprototyped behaviour change, yet it is assumed to preserve quality. Prompt drafting is scheduled for week 1 and not tested before the 25-question check, which the artifact does not say covered prompts.
attacks.evidence: "practice-area behaviour that lived in LoRA adapters moves into per-practice system prompts (drafted in week 1 by the applied team)."

attacks.claim: Embedding model change (to embed-3, 1,536 dims) means the 41M-chunk corpus must be fully re-embedded, but the plan does not say whether existing retrieval quality was measured on the new embeddings. Dual-writing new documents during re-embedding also risks index inconsistency and missing or stale chunks for tenants during week 2–4.
attacks.evidence: "re-embed corpus (~41M chunks) into Nimbus Vector Store; dual-write new documents."

attacks.claim: Rate limits are a thin margin: peak is 40 req/s against a 120 req/s contract, and the plan has no headroom analysis for bursts, multi-tenant fan-out, or re-embedding load that will run concurrently with production traffic in week 2.
attacks.evidence: "our peak is ~40 req/s; our contracted tier allows 120 req/s."

attacks.claim: Per-tenant Vector Store collections create an unbounded collection count that is not capped or load-tested; behaviour at many tenants is unknown.
attacks.evidence: "Collections are created per tenant"

attacks.claim: The savings story is not reconciled: the $7,900 generation figure is labelled an estimate with no basis shown, and the plan omits the cost of the 41M-chunk re-embedding, dual-running during migration, and any egress. Week 3 savings are also claimed from 'next billing cycle' while Nimbus charges start in week 4.
attacks.evidence: "Nimbus generation (est.)   | $0        | $7,900"

attacks.claim: Vector Store is public preview with no SLA stated, and the plan has no fallback to pgvector once it is dropped in week 5. This creates a single-vendor, pre-GA dependency on the retrieval path with no failover or observability plan.
attacks.evidence: "Moving retrieval in the same project lets us drop pgvector and its index-maintenance jobs."

attacks.claim: Latency comparison is a single 1,000-request sample from a single week, and the figure cited is p95 TTFT only, not end-to-end RAG latency including the new remote retrieval hop.
attacks.evidence: "measured at 640 ms from our Frankfurt pods (1,000 requests, week of 10-05)"

attacks.claim: Full cutover to a single managed provider for generation, embeddings, and retrieval, with models that cannot be self-hosted and fine-tuned weights deleted, creates high lock-in and exit cost with no documented export path for vectors or prompts.
attacks.evidence: "delete fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters from object storage"

attacks.claim: Tenant isolation relies solely on a tenant-scoped API key in a preview service, with no stated authz test or check that keys cannot cross tenants. Key rotation every 30 days is mentioned without a rotation runbook for the Vault injection path.
attacks.evidence: "Tenant isolation in Vector Store uses one collection per tenant with a tenant-scoped API key"

attacks.claim: Prompts and retrieved chunks containing client legal documents will be sent to a new processor; the plan does not list it as a sub-processor or confirm DPA sub-processor notification to customers.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: sub-processor update or customer notification for Nimbus

attacks.claim: Week 5 deletes pgvector and vLLM infrastructure, and week 6 is open-ended prompt tuning; there is no rollback-tested state, and deletion precedes validation.
attacks.evidence: "Week 5: remove pgvector, vLLM manifests, and GPU node pool from Terraform."

attacks.claim: Hidden quality risk: the 200k context claim may change answer behaviour for long documents, but the plan does not evaluate it, and the stated benefit is not tied to any user-facing improvement.
attacks.evidence: "Nimbus Atlas-L supports 200k context natively; our current ceiling is 32k."

attacks.claim: The stated motivation is cost and on-call pages, not customer value. The plan does not show that lawyers want the change, and the quality evidence comes from two internal reviewers.
attacks.evidence: "Atlas-L was preferred in 19 of 25 and tied in 3"

attacks.claim: Nothing
attacks.evidence: Not applicable to this infrastructure plan; no user-facing surface is changed.

attacks.claim: Nothing
attacks.evidence: No rendering or copy changes are described.

attacks.claim: Dual-write during week 2 may duplicate client document content into a second store before the EU-residency and retention questions above are resolved.
attacks.evidence: "dual-write new documents"

attacks.claim: The plan's three most material claims (quality parity, EU residency for all derived data, and cost savings) each rest on an unverified or contradicted basis, so the plan should not cross the gate in its current form.
attacks.evidence: "Vector Store ... currently provisioned in us-east-2" contradicts "all customer documents and anything derived from them ... must be processed and stored in the EU"
